key_insight: WEST is an open-source, highly scalable excited-state simulation platform that enables large, accurate GW, BSE, and TDDFT calculations without explicitly computing virtual states.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar-cell research, WEST can predict optical, excitonic, and defect-related excited-state properties at realistic material scales, supporting device design and screening.
method: Full-frequency GW, Bethe-Salpeter equation, and TDDFT in a common framework
Density functional and density matrix perturbation theory with low-rank screening/exact-exchange representations
Hierarchical parallelization and GPU acceleration for near-ideal scaling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports representative applications, including self-trapped excitons in metal-halide perovskites and simulations of systems with more than a thousand atoms.
watch_item: Performance depends on advanced parallel/GPU infrastructure and the method may still be computationally demanding for routine high-throughput use on limited resources.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
